description: SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over a user's interaction history. Item and positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting representation scores candidate items. Attention adapts the influence of recent and older interactions. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1)
motivation: Combine the simplicity of short-range transition models with the ability to capture longer dependencies. For this task, SASRec provides the starting baseline across four Amazon categories. The supplied idea specifies no additional cold-start mechanism.
implementation_notes: Start from sasrec_perdataset and retain all four dataset routes. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Select using the host's macro validation HR@10 under the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and keep predictor generation consistent with the trained architecture. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), using measured metrics and available data only.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged benchmark splits.
  Form padded history sequences and shifted next-item targets.
  Encode item and position embeddings with causal attention blocks.
  Train with positive and sampled-negative item scores.
  Save model configuration, weights, and compatible predictor.
Use host validation HR@10 averaged across the four categories for selection.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential application of self-attention to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Relative to the required SASRec baseline, this proposal supplies no new architecture, objective, or cold-start method. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Provides a foundation for testing improvements to sparse-history modeling and permitted item-content features.
future_potential.negative: Such extensions remain proposals; no validation results demonstrate improvement here. Item-ID embeddings alone do not resolve unseen-item cold start.

code_difficulty.positive: The supplied baseline already provides the core model and per-category training structure.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require matching predictor serialization and adapting diagnostic probes. Higher scores indicate greater implementation difficulty.
